findings.class: contract fidelity / add seam: a typed reference is held to a requirement's conflict rule
findings.where: scripts/orchflows_home.py import_closure.visit at 2b5b8c4e: held = pinned.get(name) or locked.get(name), applied with chain == []
findings.evidence: Before this revision add(url@v2) for a bundle the lock held at v1 and whose clone was absent replaced the lock entry (entries filtered by name, then appended). add's own already-imported refusal still says 'remove it, or edit imports.lock and run orchflows sync'. Probe P1 followed 'remove it': add v1, _discard the clone, add v2 -> RingError requires-conflict, 'team-bundle is pinned at v1 and this import needs v2 ... re-pin the bundle that asks for the older one, or drop it' -- a remedy written for a requirement author, addressed to the person who typed the reference; there is no asking bundle. No test pins either the old or the new behavior; the spec's acceptance is silent on a typed re-pin, so this is not a correctness finding against the fixed acceptance.
findings.smallest_change: one expression: held = pinned.get(name) or (locked.get(name) if chain else None), so the typed reference re-pins its own lock entry as before while a requirement still conflicts; plus one check (add @v1, remove the clone, add @v2, lock reads v2). If the refusal is the intended design instead, reword its text for chain == [] and drop 'remove it' from the already-imported refusal so the two messages agree.

findings.class: loud failure: a manifest that cannot be decoded reads as no manifest
findings.where: scripts/orchflows_bundle.py read_manifest: except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError): return None
findings.evidence: Probe P3: a BUNDLE.md whose frontmatter declares one requirement and whose body holds one Latin-1 byte returns None, so add pins the bundle with no requirements and prints no 'required' line; the contract says an absent manifest is a fact, but this manifest is present. A permission error is swallowed the same way.
findings.smallest_change: except FileNotFoundError / NotADirectoryError: return None; let UnicodeDecodeError (and any other OSError) raise rings.RingError('manifest-invalid', ...) naming the path. Three lines and one check.

findings.class: loud failure: restore keeps a lock pin that a restored manifest contradicts and says nothing
findings.where: scripts/orchflows_home.py _restored_requirements: if name in known ...: continue
findings.evidence: Probe P2: lock holds a-bundle@v1 and b-bundle@v2; a-bundle's manifest requires b-bundle@v1. restore reports both 'cloned' with no detail and the lock is unchanged. The lock is the authority on a recovery path and add would have refused this at authoring time, so keeping v2 is defensible; reporting nothing is not -- the contract promises that what restore cannot honor is 'reported against the bundle that declared it', and here it is not honored and not reported.
findings.smallest_change: pass the lock's {name: pin} instead of the name set; when a requirement's name is known and its requested pin (as written, no remote read) differs from the lock's, attach a detail to the declaring bundle's record. Five lines and one check. Same lever would let P4 name the sibling it dropped.
